caseapi.title: Advanced API security
caseapi.scenario: Two test users own different invoices in different tenants. Vulnerable mode lets Alice read Bob invoice and change a server-owned role field; fixed mode enforces ownership/tenant checks and writable-field restrictions.
caseapi.evidence: Compare owner and non-owner reads, permitted display-name changes and forbidden role updates. Record HTTP status plus actual returned fields; a successful JSON response is not sufficient proof of correct permission.
caseapi.fix: Bind identity to a validated server-side session. Apply object/tenant policy and field allowlists on every relevant route. Retire old routes explicitly and constrain list sizes.
caseapi.retest: Owner access stays 200; other-user access becomes 403; forbidden role update becomes 400 and role stays user; permitted display-name update stays 200; retired route becomes 404.
caseapi.limits: The fixture is REST only. GraphQL, API gateways, pagination across large datasets and external webhook services are design extensions, not implemented components.

caseauth.title: Authentication, sessions and federation
caseauth.scenario: The training login first issues a pending token. Vulnerable mode allows protected reads prematurely and keeps the same token after MFA; fixed mode separates stages and replaces the pending token.
caseauth.evidence: Capture the protected-route result before MFA, compare old/new token identity without publishing values, then test the old token and a logged-out token.
caseauth.fix: Enforce stage and expiry on every protected route, rotate after privilege changes and invalidate previous sessions. Federated identity additionally needs verified signatures, issuer/audience, transaction binding and a correct provider flow.
caseauth.retest: Pending and old tokens return 401; complete current tokens work; explicit logout and expiry prevent further access. The supplied tests also reject an incorrect lab MFA code.
caseauth.limits: auth_binding.py only compares synthetic state/nonce/issuer/audience. It does not implement PKCE, OAuth/OIDC, JWT signature verification, account linking, password recovery or real MFA.

caselogic.title: Business rules and concurrency
caselogic.scenario: A coupon must be redeemed once. The offline race demo deliberately schedules two reads before either update. The HTTP fixture uses a lock so concurrent requests preserve the invariant.
caselogic.evidence: The deterministic model gives two vulnerable successes and one fixed success. The HTTP regression test expects exactly one 200 and one 409 response.
caselogic.fix: Put the check and state change in one atomic operation. In multi-process production systems use appropriate database transactions/constraints; a single Python process lock does not coordinate multiple servers.
caselogic.retest: Try sequential repeats and controlled concurrency. Confirm a legitimate first redemption succeeds and the final stored state records only one redemption.
caselogic.limits: This fixture has no payments, real refunds or persistent database. Its in-memory state resets on restart and is unsuitable for production idempotency.

casereview.title: Secure code review
casereview.scenario: Trace a training request through body parsing, session validation, object lookup and response generation. Compare vulnerable and fixed branches to locate the missing security decision.
casereview.evidence: Link one observed response to the exact branch and the rule it should enforce. Use browser.js to distinguish data validation from safe output handling.
casereview.fix: Apply checks at the server boundary, use constrained input models and safe output APIs, and test both authorized and rejected paths. Framework defaults help but do not supply application-specific permissions.
casereview.retest: The regression suite must fail when the critical check is removed and pass after restoration; a clean syntax check alone is insufficient.
casereview.limits: Django snippets are review sketches that need actual models, middleware and trusted tenant context. They are not changes to your existing Django project.

casebrowser.title: Browser trust and messaging
casebrowser.scenario: The lab page accepts a specific self-message with short text. It uses an external same-origin script and a restrictive CSP. Malformed or unrelated message data is ignored.
casebrowser.evidence: Inspect the document CSP in Developer Tools, send the valid message, then send a wrong type or oversized string. Compare the visible text and the pure message-policy test results.
casebrowser.fix: Use exact expected origins, verify the intended window/source, constrain message types and fields, specify targetOrigin when sending and use safe DOM APIs. Review third-party scripts as code with origin privileges.
casebrowser.retest: Valid expected messages update text; bad type/size is ignored. Node tests additionally check wrong origin and source; manually inspect CSP in a real browser.
casebrowser.limits: Node policy tests do not exercise a browser CSP engine. Same-origin compromised scripts are already within the trust boundary; the sample does not model all DOM or cross-origin attacks.

casethreat.title: Threat modeling and trust boundaries
casethreat.scenario: Model the two-user lab before extending it with a webhook provider or admin workflow. Treat the network request, browser message and provider callback as distinct trust crossings.
casethreat.evidence: For each asset and operation record actor, entry point, trusted identity, authorization rule and downstream effect. Link each threat to at least one concrete test or review.
casethreat.fix: Mitigate at the violated boundary: object checks for invoice access, stage checks for pending sessions, atomic state changes for coupons, authenticated fresh proofs for callbacks.
casethreat.retest: Review the diagram whenever routes, identities or integrations change. Every selected mitigation should have an owner and a verification method.
casethreat.limits: The included diagram is a teaching model, not an assessment of your real network or application architecture.

caseregression.title: Automated security regression
caseregression.scenario: The lab test suite runs against temporary loopback servers and deliberately checks that fixed expectations fail against vulnerable mode. This guards against tests that merely echo implementation.
caseregression.evidence: Record test outcomes, exact app version and which assertions detect the missing control. Include successful legitimate behavior so a deny-everything change cannot pass as a fix.
caseregression.fix: Keep isolated fixtures, deterministic scheduling, explicit state resets and failures with nonzero exit. Add integration tests at the real authorization boundary when porting to a framework.
caseregression.retest: Run Python tests and the Node policy cases. Confirm the intended-negative meta-test passes because it detects failure, not because vulnerable behavior was accepted as secure.
caseregression.limits: These tests cover the synthetic app only. They do not validate a real OAuth provider, GraphQL API, browser CSP engine or deployed system.

casecapstone.title: Complete assessment and retest
casecapstone.scenario: Assess the synthetic two-user application from start to finish. Use one finding about cross-user invoice access, one authentication-state finding and one property-update finding.
casecapstone.evidence: Capture only the minimal synthetic request/response context needed to show the violated requirement. Record mode, test user, route, expected behavior, observed behavior and source location.
casecapstone.fix: Switch to the fixed implementation and inspect the policy changes. Explain why each change addresses the root cause rather than only hiding a response or renaming an identifier.
casecapstone.retest: Confirm the original unauthorized case is denied and legitimate owner access remains possible. Attach test outcomes and unresolved limitations; do not represent this as a production audit.
casecapstone.limits: The capstone is a training assessment. It contains no findings about your Django project, public sites or other systems on your network.
